overview: The National Maritime Museum Cornwall sits right on Falmouth’s harbourside and is all about the sea: boats, Cornish fishing and seafaring, and Falmouth’s own long maritime history. It’s an independent charity in a modern building opened in 2002, with 15 galleries over five floors.

It’s a great rainy-day pick in the south, and much more hands-on than the name suggests, with remote-controlled boats, a pirate play zone and an RNLI area for children, and a big changing exhibition for the grown-ups. Allow at least an hour and a half.

expect.title: Boat Hall
expect.text: You start under a flotilla of small boats hanging from the ceiling, part of a big collection of small craft.

expect.title: For children
expect.text: Steer remote-controlled boats on the Boat Pool, become a pirate in the Skull Island play zone, and clamber on rescue vehicles and dress up in the RNLI Rescue Zone.

expect.title: Under the harbour and up the tower
expect.text: The Tidal Zone takes you below the waterline to watch the harbour through big windows as the tide rises and falls, while the Lookout at the top of the tower gives views over the harbour, docks and estuary.

expect.title: Exhibitions and boatbuilding
expect.text: The Hold hosts the main temporary exhibition, and in the workshop you can watch volunteers building historic boats from scratch.

goodToKnow.label: Opening
goodToKnow.text: Open daily from 10am to 5pm, except for the three days around Christmas.

goodToKnow.label: Tickets
goodToKnow.text: Paid entry, and a standard ticket becomes an annual pass, so you can pop back free for a year. Booking online before the day saves 10%. A cheaper twilight ticket from 3pm doesn’t include the annual pass.

goodToKnow.label: Children
goodToKnow.text: Under-16s need to be with an adult.

goodToKnow.label: Parking
goodToKnow.text: The Maritime car park and Grove Place car park have more than 400 short-stay spaces within about 150 metres of the museum.

goodToKnow.label: Access
goodToKnow.text: Most floors are reached by lift or ramp; check before you go, as the tower lift (for the Tidal Zone and Lookout) has recently been out of action.

goodToKnow.label: Food
goodToKnow.text: The Waterside Café looks out over the harbour.

week.slot: One and a half to three hours
week.text: Save it for a wet day around Falmouth, and because the ticket covers a year you can come back if the weather turns again later in the week. Afterwards, wander Falmouth’s shops and harbour, or take the ferry across to St Mawes if it clears up.
